Your Description: Check if person have the permission do specific things
Refined & Easy-to-Understand Definition: Proving you are who you say you are. It's like showing your ID at a security desk.
Key Distinction: vs. Authorization: Authentication is about identity. Authorization is about permissions. You authenticate first, then you are authorized.

Your Description: The right/permission to do a specific task is granted to an entity
Refined & Easy-to-Understand Definition: The permissions you are given after you prove who you are. It's the list of rooms your keycard can open.
Key Distinction: vs. Authentication: You can't be authorized until you've been authenticated.

Your Description: Data can only be accessed by persons with the right authorization
Refined & Easy-to-Understand Definition: Keeping secrets secret. Ensuring that only the right people can see the information. Think of a sealed letter.
Key Distinction: vs. Integrity: Confidentiality is about secrecy. Integrity is about the data not being changed or tampered with.

Your Description: Information is protected from being modified by unauthorized parties
Refined & Easy-to-Understand Definition: Ensuring data is trustworthy and has not been changed. It's making sure the letter inside the sealed envelope hasn't been altered.
Key Distinction: vs. Confidentiality: A file could be public (not confidential) but still require high integrity (like a software download you don't want infected with a virus).

Your Description: Ensure information is always available to the end-user
Refined & Easy-to-Understand Definition: Ensuring that systems and data are ready and accessible when authorized users need them. It's making sure the post office is open when you need to get your letter.

Your Description: A measure of events which an entity is threatened by a potential circumstance
Refined & Easy-to-Understand Definition: The potential for loss when a threat exploits a vulnerability. Think of it as the realistic danger to your assets.
Key Distinction: vs. Threat: A threat is a potential danger (like a hurricane). Risk is the likelihood the hurricane will hit your specific house and the impact it would have.

Your Description: Circumstance or events that could cause harm to the system
Refined & Easy-to-Understand Definition: Anything that could potentially harm an asset. It's the "what could go wrong?"
Key Distinction: vs. Vulnerability: A threat is the actor or event (the burglar). A vulnerability is the weakness the threat exploits (the unlocked window).

Refined & Easy-to-Understand Definition: A weakness or gap in security that can be exploited. It's the unlocked window a burglar could climb through.
Key Distinction: vs. Threat: You can have a vulnerability (unlocked window) without a threat (no burglars in the area).

Refined & Easy-to-Understand Definition: Scrambling data using a secret key so that only authorized parties can read it. It's writing your letter in a secret code.
Key Distinction: A primary technical control used to enforce the principle of confidentiality.

Your Description: Gain people's president on policy and procedures
Refined & Easy-to-Understand Definition: Security rules for people. These are policies, procedures, and training that direct human behavior. Example: A rule stating you must lock your computer when you leave your desk.
Key Distinction: vs. Technical Control: An admin control is a rule for a person. A technical control is a setting in a machine (like the computer auto-locking after 5 minutes).
